findings.description:
`COMP_WORDS[1]` isn't normalized here, so `dvc import-url <url> <TAB>` looks up `_dvc_import-url_<url>`. `${!options_list}` then prints `invalid variable name` into the user's terminal. Normalizing only the hyphen isn't enough: `COMP_WORDS[2]` is usually a URL or path (`http://…`, `data.csv`), and those characters are invalid in a variable name too. Replacing every non-identifier character fixes both words, and an unmatched name just expands to empty:

```suggestion
      local options_list="_dvc_${COMP_WORDS[1]//[^[:alnum:]_]/_}_${COMP_WORDS[2]//[^[:alnum:]_]/_}"
```

Nit: this runs two subshells and `sed` on every TAB. It also leaves `$1` unquoted, so a word like `*` gets glob-expanded. And since this script is sourced, it adds an unprefixed `replace_hyphen` function to the user's shell. Bash's built-in parameter expansion `${COMP_WORDS[1]//-/_}` does the same job inline, so this helper could be dropped (see the suggestion on line 100 and apply the same to line 92).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Completing the argument after `dvc import-url <url>` or `dvc get-url <url>` still prints a bash `invalid variable name` error to the terminal. That's the same failure this PR fixes one word earlier.

**Reviewed changes**

I reviewed the one commit that updates the bash completion script so hyphenated commands resolve to their option variables.

- **Hyphen normalization**: adds a `replace_hyphen` helper so that `dvc import-url <TAB>` and `dvc get-url <TAB>` look up `_dvc_import_url` / `_dvc_get_url`.
- **Flag guards**: at the second and third word positions, completion now returns early when the previous word is a flag (e.g. `dvc add -R <TAB>`). Before, this produced lookups like `_dvc_add_-R`, which are invalid variable names.

I checked this by sourcing the script in bash and calling `_dvc` with a synthetic `COMP_WORDS`. `dvc import-url <TAB>` now offers `-f --file` as intended. `dvc import-url http://x <TAB>` fails with `_dvc_import-url_http://x: invalid variable name`.
